headline: No strong cause was found because there are no recent measurements [insufficient_data].
explanation: The zone is poorly served, but there are no Ookla tests in the latest quarter and data confidence is low [insufficient_data][zone_overview]. Distance to a mast does not fully explain the gap because several existing EE, Three and Vodafone sites have clear lines to many zone residents [distance_to_mast][existing_1][existing_2][existing_3]. Terrain blocks the line to every site within 5 km for only 37 people, so it affects only a small part of the zone [terrain_blocking][zone_overview]. Only about 0.1 operators have approximate sites within 5 km, but unknown operators do not mean a single operator and no operator coverage is confirmed at the point [single_operator][zone_overview].

fix_plan.why: The zone has thin data: no Ookla tests in the latest quarter and low data confidence [zone_overview]; the fix rule says measure first to confirm [fix_rule]. Once measured, cand_1 is the best new-site candidate because it gives the most zone residents a clear line: 873 poorly served people in all [cand_1].
assumptions: line of sight to cell centres, not a radio model
fix_plan.candidate_finding: Candidate 1: a new 25 m mast on high ground (132 m, inside the zone) would give 873 of the zone's people a clear line of sight (873 poorly served people in all; 4294 people reached in 27 of 45 cells checked).

review.reason: The plan correctly uses the zone's people gaining (873 poorly served) from [cand_1], states assumptions, matches the fix_rule's measure-first guidance for thin data [zone_overview][fix_rule], and flags low data confidence.

limitations: Sites are approximate; antenna heights assumed; Ofcom figures are area-level; no Ookla tests in the latest quarter so measurements are needed before a cause can be confirmed [insufficient_data][fix_rule].

critiques.reason: The zone overview explicitly states there are no Ookla tests in the latest quarter and data confidence is low, and the fix rule confirms zero tests in the zone, so measurements are needed before confirming any cause.

The zone overview shows 836 people have no identified site within 5 km, but existing sites (EE, Three, Vodafone) at 4.2–5.9 km reach hundreds of zone residents with clear lines of sight, so distance is a factor for many but does not fully explain the gap for all.
Only 37 people are terrain-blocked to every site within 5 km per the zone overview, while existing sites provide clear lines to hundreds, confirming terrain affects only a small portion of the zone.

The zone overview reports an average of 0.1 operators have approximate sites within 5 km of its cells (EE, Three somewhere nearby) [zone_overview], but 'operators unknown' does not equate to a single operator, and no operator coverage is confirmed at the point; the low confidence appropriately reflects this weak evidence.

The plan correctly uses the zone's people gaining (873 poorly served) from [cand_1], states assumptions, matches the fix_rule's measure-first guidance for thin data [zone_overview][fix_rule], and flags low data confidence.
